extracted.intended_audience: communications and PR professionals; measurement and evaluation specialists
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for planning, measuring, and evaluating communications and PR activity, as set out in Barcelona Principles 3.0 (AMEC). Intended to inform goal-setting, methods, scope, and ethical practice in communications measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. Setting goals is an absolute prerequisite to communications planning, measurement, and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.description: The founding principle of SMART (specific, measurable, actionable, relevant, and time-bound) goals as a foundation for communications planning has been promoted to an essential prerequisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals must be defined before measurement and evaluation; they articulate target outcomes and how progress will be assessed. Use SMART goals so measurement is built into planning rather than retrofitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. Measurement and evaluation should identify outputs, outcomes, and potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously, the Principles recommended measuring outcomes, rather than simply counting outputs. The updated principles extend this to consider longer term impact of communications strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement should move beyond counts (outputs) to demonstrate outcomes (changes in awareness, attitudes, behaviour) and where possible potential/longer-term impact. Avoid relying solely on activity metrics without linking them to intended effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. Outcomes and impact should be identified for stakeholders, society, and the organization.
rubrics_metrics.description: From the original focus on business metrics, such as sales and revenue, the 2020 update embraces a more holistic view of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define whose outcomes and impacts you are measuring — include stakeholders, wider society, and the organization itself. This broadens applicability to non-profit and non-commercial communications roles and acknowledges multiple beneficiary groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. Communication measurement and evaluation should include both qualitative and quantitative analysis.
rubrics_metrics.description: “To understand the full impact of your work, it is crucial that you use the full suite of methods to measure those outcomes,” summarised Ben Levine AMEC Board Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine quantitative metrics (reach, impressions, conversions) with qualitative methods (message testing, sentiment, interpretation) to understand how messages are received, believed and interpreted. Don’t rely exclusively on numbers—context and meaning matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5. AVEs are not the value of communication.
rubrics_metrics.description: “We continue to believe that AVEs do not demonstrate the value of our work.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising Value Equivalents (AVEs) should not be used as a proxy for communications value. Employ richer, nuanced, multi-faceted approaches to understand impact rather than using AVEs as a valuation metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6. Holistic communication measurement and evaluation includes all relevant online and offline channels.
rubrics_metrics.description: Our founding principle that social media can and should be measured is so obvious today. The 2020 iteration reflects the game-changing shift in social communications’ capabilities, opportunities, and influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure earned, owned, shared, and paid channels consistently; include both online and offline channels equally. Ensure clarity across channels and a consistent approach aligned to common goals rather than privileging one medium over others.

rubrics_metrics.name: 7. Communication measurement and evaluation are rooted in integrity and transparency to drive learning and insights.
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound, consistent, and sustained measurement calls for integrity and transparency in recognition of today’s attention to data privacy and stewardship as organisations comply with new regulations, such as GDPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about context, methodologies, tools, biases, and data stewardship. Focus measurement on learning and applying insights back into planning, and ensure ethical handling of data (privacy, consent, compliance).
